acceptanceCriteria.statement: Real-unit inputs (planet radius_km, per-feature horizontal size_km, relief height_km) are converted into the shader's unit-sphere uniforms via named single-source helpers defined once in planet-lod-lab-core.js — featureFrequencyFromKm (= C_feature * radius_km / size_km), reliefAmplitudeFromKm (= height_km / radius_km), reliefGravityFactor(surfaceGravity), animationRateFactor(radius_km), plus R_EARTH_KM — and INVOKED from the lab's uniform-build path (applyDrivers / the uniform .value assignments in planet-lod-lab.html), per the AC8-blessed single-source architecture (the helpers are not literally inlined inside deriveUniforms()). The per-feature (C_feature, featureSize_km) calibration is set so already-good features keep ~current frequency at the reference radius, while Max-flagged-oversized features (craters, rivers) calibrate to a smaller footprint (higher base frequency).

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run tests/planet-scale.test.js (helper property oracle) + tests/planet-scale-calibration.test.js (calibration guard): sample each helper across radius_km 0.3..16 RE and a feature size_km sweep; pin the crater/river calibrated inputs against their documented pre-change baselines
verifyVia.observable: frequency monotonically increases with radius_km and decreases with size_km, bounded; amplitude == height_km/radius_km; rate ~ 1/radius_km; reliefGravityFactor monotonic-decreasing in surfaceGravity within [floor,ceil]; calibration guard: at RE=1 crater base frequency (≈12.0) and river base frequency (=4.6) are each strictly GREATER than their documented pre-change defaults (crater 6.0, river 2.3) — smaller footprint; both suites green

acceptanceCriteria.amended: 2026-06-17 (Max-approved): reworded to match the AC8-blessed single-source architecture — helpers are defined once in planet-lod-lab-core.js and invoked from the uniform-build path (applyDrivers / uniform .value assignments), not literally inside deriveUniforms(); calibration clause now backed by tests/planet-scale-calibration.test.js. Intent and requirement unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Raising the planet-radius dial at a fixed feature size_km visibly shrinks and multiplies craters/rivers; and on an Earth-sized Rocky world the flagged features (craters, rivers) occupy a clearly smaller fraction of the disk than the pre-change baseline ('no longer makes the planet look small').

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223, Rocky preset d4 clouds zeroed: screenshot at radius 1.0 before/after the change; then sweep the radius dial up (e.g. 1.0 -> 3.0) holding crater size_km, screenshot pair
verifyVia.observable: After-shot craters/rivers occupy a visibly smaller disk-fraction than before (pixel-diff >=3%, measured feature angular size down); radius-up sweep shows smaller + more numerous craters

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Relief features are authored as a height in km; the rendered relief amplitude = height_km/radius_km, with the authored height capped by reliefGravityFactor so low-gravity worlds (Mars/Titan) show exaggerated relief and high-gravity worlds (Magma/Carbon) show subdued relief.

verifyVia.input: vitest: relief-amplitude factor across all 23 presets ordered by surfaceGravity. Live: :9223 grazing sun angle, Mars/Titan before/after + a high-g vs low-g comparator
verifyVia.observable: Oracle: Mars/Titan resolve to higher effective relief than Magma/Carbon, monotonic in gravity, bounded. Live: Mars/Titan after-shots show deeper relief shadows than before; high-g world reads visibly flatter

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Time-driven features slow down on large bodies via animationRateFactor ~ 1/radius_km: lava emissive 'breathing' on Lava/Magma is visibly slower than pre-change, and gas-giant storm drift on a large giant (Jovian r11.2) is slower than on a smaller giant (Neptune r3.9).

verifyVia.input: Lab on :9223: Lava nightside, sample uTime-advanced frames N apart, measure crack-glow phase delta before/after; Jovian vs Neptunian storm centroid displacement over equal uTime
verifyVia.observable: Lava crack-glow phase advances less per unit time than pre-change; Jovian storm centroid moves less than Neptune's over equal uTime

acceptanceCriteria.statement: On preset load a generic-archetype preset draws a seeded random radius from the game's radiusRangesEarth for its type; a reroll button/seed redraws; named real bodies (Mars, Titan, Hot Jupiter, Venus, Europa, Magma, ...) default to a canonical-size lock; a manual radius slider overrides any of these.

verifyVia.input: vitest: for each preset, derived radiusEarth lands within its archetype range (or equals canonical for named bodies). Live: :9223 reroll on a generic preset changes the radius readout + feature footprints; named body stays canonical
verifyVia.observable: Oracle: every draw in-range / named-body canonical; suite green. Live: reroll visibly changes radius + footprint; manual slider override takes effect
